source_title: Bellbrook's battle with invasive flying fox camps
evidence_description: Independent press report of the 20 May 2025 Kempsey Shire Council ordinary meeting: Paul Hodgson (Bellbrook Hall and Progress Association) presented a Flying-fox Camp Management Plan support request; council stated it "simply does not have the budget to tackle the issue"; council indicated it hoped to revisit the matter at the October 2025 meeting and agreed to meet with residents and stakeholders. No resolution number or vote count reported.
relevant_quotation: Kempsey Shire Council... simply does not have the budget to tackle the issue.
investigation_relevance: The single independently-fetched, non-operator-supplied source in this case for the May 2025 meeting. Corroborates the account in SRC-0005, SRC-0007, SRC-0008, SRC-0011; does not corroborate SRC-0006's resolution-number and vote-count claims. Core evidence for CTR-0001.

source_title: Rudder Park Flying-fox Camp Management Plan completion
evidence_description: Kempsey Shire Council's only completed Flying-fox Camp Management Plan covers Rudder Park, East Kempsey, completed in 2022 (SRC-0007 specifies July 2022). Council has no completed or draft plan for Bellbrook.
relevant_quotation: Kempsey Shire Council has a completed management plan for one site: Rudder Park in East Kempsey. That plan was completed in 2022.
investigation_relevance: Central to the Documented Compliance vs. Functional Compliance pattern in this case: a real governance instrument exists and has worked for one site in the same shire, while Bellbrook remains without one.

source_title: Planning docs, Councillor fees and progress on a statue for Dave Sands (May 2025 Council meeting wrap)
hash_exception_reason: Council site returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; content known only from a search-engine snippet.
evidence_description: Search-snippet indicates two Notices of Motion passed at the May 2025 meeting, one described as providing Bellbrook with more information about managing the colony. This is a real formal action, but a narrower one than SRC-0006's claim of a substantive investigate-and-report-back resolution with a recorded vote.
relevant_quotation: Two Notices of Motion were passed at the May Council meeting... providing the Bellbrook with more information about managing a bat colony currently inhabiting their town.
investigation_relevance: Sits between the two competing accounts of the meeting - confirms something beyond a flat refusal was formally moved and passed, without confirming SRC-0006's specific resolution numbers or vote count. Central to CTR-0001.

source_title: Kempsey Shire Council written advocacy update to Bellbrook residents
evidence_description: 18 March 2026 letter signed by Caro Szary, Group Manager Strategic and Asset Planning, describing: correspondence to NSW DCCEEW and Mid North Coast Local Health District; the 2025 community meeting and resident visits; camp monitoring; a letter of support to Bellbrook Public School; an intention to seek external grants; and a request to Michael Kemp MP for state-level support. States council is waiting on a response from state agencies. Discloses no outcome, no confirmed grant application, and no commitment to develop a management plan.
investigation_relevance: The clearest documentary instance of the case's central pattern: council's own letter describes activity, not outcome. The letter itself has not been independently obtained by this investigation - it is described consistently across two operator-supplied documents, not sighted directly.

source_title: Absence of Bellbrook flying-fox item from October 2025 council agenda
evidence_description: Council indicated at the 20 May 2025 meeting it hoped to revisit the Bellbrook flying-fox matter in October 2025. No item on the matter appears in the October 2025 agenda or confirmed minutes. The Hardened Submission Package extends this to November, December 2025 and February 2026 meeting cycles as well, and frames it as non-execution of an affirmative resolution rather than simply a missed informal commitment - that framing is not corroborated (see CTR-0001), but the underlying October absence is consistent across every document that addresses it.
relevant_quotation: the matter did not appear on the October 2025 agenda
investigation_relevance: Independent of how the May 2025 meeting itself is characterised, this specific claim - nothing on Bellbrook flying-fox in the October agenda - is the most consistently repeated fact in the whole document set.

source_title: Council Submission - Bellbrook Flying Fox, June 2026
evidence_description: Draft letter to Kempsey Shire Council CEO Andrew Meddle, five direct questions: whether council will commit to a management plan; explanation for the October agenda omission; what the August/September 2025 consultation produced; status of any grant application; and status of responses from NSW DCCEEW and the Local Health District. States the submission is intended to go simultaneously to state and federal representatives and the NSW Ombudsman.
relevant_quotation: Will council commit to developing a Flying-fox Camp Management Plan for Bellbrook?
investigation_relevance: Not confirmed as sent - drafted with an unsigned signature block as at 2026-08-22. Represents the advocacy chain's intended next step, not yet a completed action.

source_title: Ombudsman Complaint - Bellbrook Flying Fox, June 2026
evidence_description: Draft formal complaint to the NSW Ombudsman under the Ombudsman Act 1974 (NSW). Uses the SRC-0001-consistent account of the May 2025 meeting (declined on budget, hoped to revisit October). Seeks investigation of council's conduct, production of the August/September 2025 consultation document chain, explanation for the October omission, and a formal statement on whether council intends to develop a plan.
relevant_quotation: council's conduct in relation to Bellbrook flying fox management constitutes unreasonable, unjust, or otherwise defective conduct
investigation_relevance: Not confirmed as lodged - drafted with an unsigned signature block as at 2026-08-22. The most detailed and best-corroborated of the advocacy drafts.

source_title: Bellbrook Flying-Fox Droppings — What's Actually Established
evidence_description: Histoplasmosis (a fungal lung/bloodstream infection from inhaling spores in accumulated droppings) is a real, medically documented mechanism. Standard "living near a flying-fox camp is low risk" council/NSW Health messaging is calibrated for distant colonies with no droppings contact - not for roofs, gutters and yards under direct heavy accumulation. No lab test has confirmed Histoplasma capsulatum in this specific colony's droppings; that would require environmental sampling not yet done. The document explicitly frames the messaging gap as a scope limitation, not a claim about anyone's intent, and notes an absence of confirmed local cases does not mean no mild/undiagnosed infections have occurred - clinical literature cited puts undiagnosed rates as high as 90% in immunocompetent people.
relevant_quotation: The illness mechanism is real; the source confirmation isn't there yet.
investigation_relevance: The health-risk dimension of the case, self-hedged at the source to distinguish established mechanism from unconfirmed local instance - matches this project's own evidentiary standard already.

source_title: Council website classification of Bellbrook camp as 'historic'
evidence_description: The media pitch document states council's website classifies Bellbrook as a 'historic' flying-fox camp while residents live with an actively occupied one. Not mentioned in any of the other seven documents; not yet independently checked against the council's actual camp register or NSW Government's Flying-fox Camp Database.
relevant_quotation: council website classification of Bellbrook as a 'historic' camp while residents live with an active one
investigation_relevance: If confirmed, this would be a direct structural parallel to the case's central Documented Compliance vs. Functional Compliance pattern - a documented classification not matching functional reality - but it currently rests on a single unverified source and must not be treated as established.

evidence_description: Claims that Resolution 2025.79 (extending meeting hours) and Resolution 2025.80 (passed 9/0, directing executive investigation of Level 1 management options and a report back by the October meeting) were passed at the 20 May 2025 meeting, with a shire-wide-alignment amendment defeated 2/7. No other document in this case, including independently-fetched EV-0001, mentions any resolution number or vote count. A targeted search for these specific resolution numbers found no corroboration; the council's own site and web.archive.org both blocked automated fetch of the primary minutes, so this has not been ruled in or out against the primary record.
investigation_relevance: The load-bearing claim for the Hardened Submission Package's SafeWork NSW and Office of Local Government submissions (Part 5), which characterise the failure as non-execution of an affirmative unanimous directive rather than a discretionary refusal. This is a materially stronger claim than the rest of the case supports as things stand. Do not use in any public-facing material until verified against the actual signed minutes. See CTR-0001, Q-0001.

source_title: NSW flying-fox grants program is plan-gated
evidence_description: The NSW Government holds approximately $1 million for councils managing flying-fox camp impacts. Access requires a completed or draft Camp Management Plan for the specific site. Without a plan, a site is not eligible - meaning Bellbrook cannot lawfully receive plan-gated funding regardless of any grant application council makes, unless directed to Rudder Park (the only site with a plan).
relevant_quotation: A Camp Management Plan is the access mechanism for state funding. Without a plan, a site is not eligible.
investigation_relevance: This is the case's core structural finding: a real remedy mechanism exists, gated behind a single document council has declined to produce. Not yet independently confirmed against the NSW Government's own grant program guidelines.

source_title: Level 1/Level 2 management actions available without a licence
evidence_description: Described consistently across two independently-toned documents: the NSW Flying-fox Camp Management Code of Practice 2018 pre-approves certain Level 1 (routine site management, hygiene cleaning, signage) and Level 2 (vegetation buffer creation, branch trimming) interventions without individual licensing, subject to welfare-based scheduling conditions (e.g. trimming after animals depart to forage). Protected-species status prevents dispersal or lethal control; it does not prevent these actions.
relevant_quotation: The legal protection applies to harming the bats. It does not apply to protecting the community from the harm the bats cause.
investigation_relevance: Directly undercuts any framing that legal protection alone explains council's inaction - the two documents differ sharply in how they characterise council's conduct (CTR-0001) but agree on what the Code of Practice actually permits. Not yet checked against the primary Code of Practice document itself.
